minor.issue: Double-DELETE returns 200 instead of 404 for a not-found image. Root cause: server.py L3170-3180 uses `$pull` alongside `$set: updated_at` in same update op. Since $set always bumps updated_at, `modified_count` is always 1 even when $pull matched no image, so the `modified_count == 0 → 404` check never triggers. Fix: check `pre.count` vs `post.count` or use find_one_and_update and inspect the array.

action_items: Fix double-DELETE image endpoint so it returns 404 when the image doesn't exist (issue detailed above). Very minor — everything else on Sprint 3 is green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to 3357 lines. Sprint 3 added ~430 more (rooms + share + public + generate-overview). The extraction recommendation from iteration_5 still stands — please extract rooms into /app/backend/rooms.py (models, helpers, router) before Sprint 4 to keep this file navigable.

generate_overview gates on `EMERGENT_LLM_KEY and ENABLE_REAL_PRODUCTS` — the AND with ENABLE_REAL_PRODUCTS is surprising. If a designer flips off ENABLE_REAL_PRODUCTS globally to disable Sprint 2 catalogue calls, they also silently lose real AI overview (fall back to boilerplate). Consider a separate ENABLE_REAL_OVERVIEW flag or just gate on EMERGENT_LLM_KEY alone.

Public endpoint /api/public/rooms/{slug} does NOT validate `slug` shape — Mongo query is safe but a malicious client could hammer the endpoint with random slugs for enumeration. Consider adding a light regex `^[a-z0-9]{6,14}$` and returning 400 on malformed slug (still 404 on unknown).

In PATCH /rooms/{id}, `updates['concept_overview'] = payload.concept_overview[:4000]` silently truncates — no error is surfaced to UI. For designer trust, prefer 400 on >4000 chars with an explicit message, or expose the effective length back in the response.

_make_slug uses secrets.token_urlsafe(9) then strips `_-` and lowercases; strip could occasionally shorten a slug below 6 chars (test bound is 6-14 but in edge cases you can get less). Consider looping until len >= 8 to guarantee entropy.

rca of the issue: Double-DELETE image bug root cause is a single-write mongo op combining $pull and $set. When $pull is a no-op, $set on updated_at still increments modified_count, defeating the 404 guard. Reproduction: (1) upload image to a room, (2) delete it — 200, (3) delete the same img_id again — expected 404, actual 200. Mitigation: split into a read-then-write (verify the image exists first via find_one and array projection, then run the $pull-only update); or run $pull without touching updated_at and add a separate updated_at write only when modified_count>0.
